question: how many compiled rules gain a factor as their source, on what evidence, per cell type

evidence_kinds.occupancy_same_cell_with_motif: measured occupancy in the rule's own cell, with the factor's own JASPAR profile matching inside the element; occupancy is not function
evidence_kinds.occupancy_same_cell: measured occupancy in the rule's own cell, no match of the factor's profile (or no profile); possibly indirect; occupancy is not function
evidence_kinds.occupancy_other_cell: measured occupancy only in other cell types: not a source in the rule's cell and never emitted there
evidence_kinds.motif_only: predicted: a JASPAR match and no occupancy anywhere; a motif is not occupancy
evidence_kinds.unknown: no evidence of either kind: the source stays UNKNOWN

compile_spec: compile.py would read the git-ignored assignment table this lane writes (data/cache/regulators/assignment.tsv.gz: one row per compiled rule and factor occupying its element in the rule's own cell) and, per program: (1) declare one gene stub per factor it uses, as it declares target genes, so the factor is an entity a rule can name; (2) for each row whose direction is activates or inhibits, emit `rule <FACTOR> <direction> <GENE> { through: <element>; when: cell_type = <cell>; evidence: measured "ENCODE TF ChIP-seq peak cluster, <cell>" occupancy, not function; direction: curated GO term, factor-level }`, one rule per element, as v0.5 requires; (3) state no `strength:` it does not have. Two engine facts block a faithful emission today, and neither is compile.py's to change: the parser reads `strength` only as a number and a rule with no strength runs at 1.0 (genomeos/ir/model.py), so an unmeasured factor effect would run at full strength; and a row whose direction is unknown has no grammar token (Albert's decision queue, 'a grammar token for an unresolved direction'), so it must not be emitted as activates or inhibits. Until both are decided, the honest emission is the evidence as a comment, or a `binds` rule, which takes no `through` and runs nothing.
example_directed_rule: rule CTCF inhibits SAMD11 { through: EH38E2776632; when: cell_type = transverse_colon; evidence: measured "ENCODE TF ChIP-seq peak cluster, transverse_colon" occupancy, not function; direction curated repressor at an element whose compiled rule inhibits the gene }

assignment_table.columns: program element gene cell rule_action factor kind motif occupied_in_cells direction direction_basis

reading: a rule gains a source when at least one factor has a ChIP-seq peak cluster over its element in the rule's own cell type: measured occupancy, which is not function. Only the cell types ENCODE profiled can gain one; every other rule keeps an UNKNOWN source whatever its motifs
money: none: no request is sent and no key is read

sources.version: the files on this machine, pinned by sha256 in inputs

inputs.path: JASPAR matches per compiled element, cached

result_manifest.assembly: GRCh38 for the compiled elements, the peak clusters and the reference sequence

parameters.no_expression_read: the census opens no expression, perturbation or model value

result_manifest.partitions: n/a: every compiled rule is counted

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record cfc30e4

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
